title: ETL command preparation after one existing connection retarget
candidate: source-only retained range receipt and sparse sorted bucket update

methods.settling: Each real forward/restored public API retarget is followed by the first requestAnimationFrame callback, at least 100 ms since input, and two further requestAnimationFrame callbacks. Pointer is outside the graph; Live and MiniMap are off.
methods.operation: g.api.updateConnection(existingEdgeId, {targetBlockId, targetAnchorId}); alternate target and original target are distinct, valid, resolved blocks/anchors. No add, delete, selection or artificial backend invalidation.
methods.timing: Top-level inclusive performance.now timers only. inputToRaf is elapsed time until the first rAF callback resumes, not physical input-to-photon. draw is the backend portion; scheduler includes draw and must not be added to it. No CPU profiler, GC tracing or allocation sampling in headline runs.
methods.summary: Median is arithmetic median, averaging the middle observations for even n. p95 is sorted[floor(0.95*n)], capped at n-1. Durations are milliseconds. Raw rows rounded to 6 decimals.
methods.quality: Full main WebGL framebuffer readPixels RGBA, fixed frame time 2.5, same fixture/camera/operation. Excludes composited HTML and any MiniMap. All 12 reference/candidate pairs are compared byte-for-byte. Four before/forward/restored triplets establish that mutation is visible and reversible.
methods.gpu: Sparse EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 samples; GPU-disjoint results omitted. These are a guard, not a dense per-operation latency estimate.
methods.cameraGuard: One measured 160-frame logarithmic .01→.95→.01 cycle after a complete 160-frame warm cycle, each build.
methods.liveGuard: Same real ETL Storybook simulation tick(10) every 500 ms, Live enabled, MiniMap disabled. 300 rAF samples per build in one unbalanced guard. Tick counter spans run warmup/drain as well as measured frames; only five measured frames draw. Not a new balanced Live benchmark.
methods.memory: Resident path capacities, ordering numeric arrays and overlap typed buffers are recorded before/after warmed retarget samples. This is not a full retained-heap/GC measurement and excludes JavaScript container overhead.
methods.serialization: All browser jobs use the shared Chromium lock. Parent and peers held heavy CPU tasks and Storybook edits during final acquisition.

diagnostic.nestedTimingCaveat: Inclusive nested timers plus CPU/GC tracing are attribution only, not comparable headline timings.
diagnostic.confirmedBottleneck: ETL cachedSourceBuckets median 9.05 ms, forEachRange 6.85 ms, sortBuckets 1.9 ms; filterTranslucentRuns 4.25 ms in the separately instrumented diagnostic. Scheduler residual was about 1.2 ms.
diagnostic.coverageDecision: Rejected: same-state ABBA base medians 4.35/4.00 ms versus coverage 4.40/3.70 ms did not establish a useful improvement. Exact output tuples matched. It is absent from the final bundle.

limitations: ETL order preparation improves, but visibility filtering and path upload preparation remain material CPU work and are slower in some candidate passes.
Nirvana has no active translucent ordering workload in this fixture. Its result is a control, not evidence of a new Nirvana optimization.
Candidate B1 and B2 differ materially; both per-run summaries and pooled results are retained. No warmup-only subset is discarded.
The small Live guard still has approximately 70–80 ms draw bursts. This change does not solve general Live update latency.

Temporary local paths identify original evidence; they are not portable runtime dependencies. To repeat elsewhere, freeze an identical fixture for both builds and use the public API operation and explicit settings above.
Source-only candidate does not change shaders, geometry packing, camera LOD, AA, style semantics or primitive ordering. All rejected visibility/command-packing ideas are excluded.
